summary: Embedding bit-depth ramp in proxy causing quiet top-k and occasional serialization warnings
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden drop in reranker recall and low-scoring top-k candidates for certain queries. Symptoms started after a proxy config rollout. Impact: ClearDocs production pipelines see ~18% drop in top-5 recall and elevated rerank tail latency due to retries. Environment: Dedicated tenant on us-east, using rwd-open-embedding-001 served via edge proxy (version 2026.03.08).

Observed behavior: - Embeddings arriving at rerank service sometimes show reduced dynamic range (values clustered near 0), causing cosine similarity suppression. - Proxy logs contain periodic serialization warnings about 'unsupported numeric bit-depth' near the same timestamps. - Re-running the same payload directly against the serving runtime (bypassing proxy) returns expected float32 embeddings and restores rerank quality.

Urgency: Customer production degradation, P1 expected response.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send the customer's sample batch (attached) through the repro proxy route via POST /v1/embeddings with content-type application/json.
2) Observe embedding vector numeric ranges in response and compare against direct runtime endpoint (/private-runtime/embeddings).
3) Run rerank job using supplied vectors and check top-5 recall.
4) Compare proxy logs for serialization warnings at timestamps.

Notes: Repro was intermittent (~1/6 batches) but consistent when proxy used; bypass reliably produces correct vectors.
logs:
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] proxy-frontend WARN serialization: unsupported numeric bit-depth: 16 -> falling back to approximate encode
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] proxy-frontend DEBUG payload-size=12kb tenant=cleardocs route=/v1/embeddings
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] rerank INFO cosine_top5=0.12 (expected ~0.62) latency=142ms
[2026-03-09T18:12:05Z] runtime DEBUG embed-response dtype=float32 first_val=0.12345
[2026-03-09T18:12:05Z] proxy DEBUG downstream-encode dtype=uint16 sample_first_val=3
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Recent proxy optimization introduced a ‘bit-depth ramp’ that attempts lower-bit quant storage for in-flight embeddings to save bandwidth. Evidence: proxy logs explicitly mention 'unsupported numeric bit-depth: 16' and downstream encode shows uint16 values. Direct runtime returns float32.
Actions taken: - Reproduced locally with customer's payload and confirmed proxy-encoded embeddings are effectively quantized to uint16 in wire format, losing sign and magnitude. - Confirmed rerank algorithm expects float32 normalized embeddings; quantization without proper dequant/scale leads to compressed vectors near zero. - SRE examined last proxy rollout (2026-03-08) which included middleware change 'embed-compress' to enable bandwidth savings for large tenants.
Open questions: Was embed-compress intended to be tenant-gated? Why did telemetry not flag drift earlier?

resolution_notes:
Workaround: Temporary bypass rule added for tenant 'cleardocs' on proxy (2026-03-10 10:12) which restored expected embedding values.
Fix: Hotfix deployed to proxy (v2026.03.12-hotfix-embed) with three changes: 1) feature flag scoping to ensure embed-compress is tenant-gated; 2) include X-Embed-Scale header and dtype metadata to allow downstream dequantization; 3) validation to reject quantized payloads without scale header.
Rollout notes: Hotfix rolled to us-east prod first; metrics show top-5 recall recovered to baseline within 20 minutes.
Postmortem actions: - Create Confluence runbook 'Embedding Serialization Runbook' (link added). - Add alert for embedding dynamic-range drop in Console (token-level). - Audit ClearDocs traffic for the past 72 hours and offer support for any affected rerank jobs. - Add integration test covering proxy encode/decode roundtrip for embeddings.
Status: Resolved for customer; follow-ups scheduled (runbook, audit).
